minutes.headline: Finance Committee voted recommendations on all 15 special town meeting articles; Parks will pass over Marshall Park borrowing.
minutes.summary: The committee held a public hearing on the special town meeting warrant with the interim town manager, then voted a recommendation on each article. The Parks Commission said the Marshall Park cost estimate rose so far that it will ask town meeting to pass over its borrowing article. The Municipal Building Design Committee gave an update, and members were assigned liaison roles.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted a recommendation on each article of the special town meeting warrant, mostly approval or no financial impact.
The committee recommended deferral on Article 1, the FY25 budget amendment, and on Articles 14 and 15, which are to be passed over.
Salary administration plan amendments one and two (Articles 11 and 12) were recommended 4-1; the committee recommended approval of Articles 2 through 6 and Article 9.
The Parks Commission said the new Marshall Park cost estimate is far above earlier ones, so existing money cannot fund phase one and it will seek to pass over its borrowing article.
The committee held its public hearing on the warrant, then assigned liaison roles and set no November meeting; the next regular meeting is in the second week of December.

why_it_matters: The recommendations shape how residents are likely to be asked to vote at special town meeting on the FY25 budget amendment, school aid, the salary plan and new revolving funds.
Part-time holiday pay and prorated leave would be paid mostly from existing budgets, which reduces free cash rather than adding a new appropriation.
Marshall Park's phase one is not funded by existing money, so the project's cost and timing remain open.
watch_next: The special town meeting vote on the 15 warrant articles, including whether Article 1 and the Marshall Park borrowing article are passed over.
The next regular Finance Committee meeting in the second week of December.
